question: Can dense MLP and spiking-network weight matrices be replaced by a low-dimensional spatial wiring rule whose neuron coordinates are learned?

key_findings.claim: Inverse-distance wiring reduces trainable parameter scaling from quadratic in neuron count to linear while retaining a dense computed connectivity matrix.
key_findings.evidence: Each neuron learns two in-layer coordinates, a bias, and an excitatory/inhibitory mask; connection weights are reciprocal Euclidean distances, so the 2,048-hidden-unit 3D MLP has 10,576 parameters but more than 1.6 million computed connections.

key_findings.claim: The spatial MLP is parameter-efficient but does not beat parameter-matched conventional MLPs on unpruned MNIST.
key_findings.evidence: The 3D MLP reaches 0.9217 plus or minus 0.0024, below a 14-hidden-unit baseline at 0.9429 and a full 2,048-unit baseline at 0.9745; relaxing z coordinates raises it to 0.9337 but remains below its matched baseline.

key_findings.claim: Spatial models become relatively competitive under severe magnitude pruning, especially for spiking networks.
key_findings.evidence: The 3D MLP overtakes the small matched-parameter MLP above 80% post-training pruning and the large baseline at 95%; the 3D SNN reaches 0.9216 versus 0.9031 for its parameter-matched small SNN.

method.core_idea: Represent each neuron by a learned Euclidean position and derive all inter-layer weights from reciprocal distance plus a learned neuron-level sign.
method.mechanism: Gradient descent moves neurons, so one coordinate update jointly changes all incident weights; fixed or learned layer distances preserve feed-forward computation, and long connections can be pruned as small weights.
assumptions: A low-dimensional metric geometry can express the task's useful weight correlations.
A single sign per neuron is sufficient for excitatory versus inhibitory effects.
Computed dense weights are affordable even when stored trainable parameters are few.

techniques.role: Compresses a dense matrix into learned neuron coordinates and a fixed inverse-distance decoder.
Restores negative connections within an otherwise positive distance rule.
Deletes long, weak connections using the geometry itself.

evaluations.setting: Three-layer MLPs on MNIST across three seeds
evaluations.metric: Test accuracy and trainable parameter count

evaluations.result: Relative advantage appears only at high sparsity and depends on baseline size.
evaluations.baseline: Conventional MLPs with matched parameters or neurons

limitations: Only MNIST and shallow fully connected networks are tested.
Trainable storage is reduced, but dense distance computation does not automatically reduce inference FLOPs.
Moving one neuron couples every incident weight and limits expressivity; higher embedding dimensions improve accuracy but add parameters.
failure_modes: Neuron collisions make reciprocal weights numerically large.
The shared geometry cannot independently tune incident connections.
A fixed excitatory/inhibitory sign per neuron cannot express arbitrary signed matrices.
reusable_insights: Separate trainable-description complexity from the number and cost of computed connections.
Geometric weight generators yield interpretable structured compression and a natural pruning order.
Parameter-matched and compute-matched baselines answer different efficiency questions and both are needed.
open_questions: Does coordinate-generated convolution or attention remain competitive on CIFAR/ImageNet at matched latency?
Which bounded distance kernels avoid singularities while retaining compression?
Can learned sparse neighborhoods deliver actual hardware savings rather than parameter savings alone?

competitive_landscape.title: Spatially embedded recurrent neural networks reveal widespread links between structural and functional neuroscience findings
competitive_landscape.difference: Achterberg et al. regularize fixed network weights using spatial wiring cost; this paper makes positions the optimized parameters and deterministically decodes weights from them.

competitive_landscape.title: Complex computation from developmental priors
competitive_landscape.difference: Developmental priors generate connectivity through compact rules; inverse-distance position optimization uses a much simpler differentiable geometry and evaluates parameter compression directly.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning both Weights and Connections for Efficient Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Han et al. learn then prune individual weights; the spatial model never stores independent weights and prunes by a shared geometric generator.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: spatial constraints, developmental wiring rules, and pruning predate this work. Its distinctive step is optimizing neuron coordinates as the sole generator of dense signed weights for both MLPs and SNNs, with explicit parameter-count comparisons.
reviewer_notes: Full methods, tables, pruning regimes, discussion, and conclusion were checked. Parameter efficiency should not be read as demonstrated compute or energy efficiency. Competitor primary records checked 2026-08-23.
